message.content: {"A0100":"A0100 spent the first half of the window descending and accelerating northward with A0200, closing the southbound B formation rather than maneuvering for separation. When its missile count fell and an A0100 missile appeared at 9.4 seconds, it began a sustained hard right turn while continuing down, carrying it east of the original approach line; this most plausibly was a post-launch crank or defensive break to reduce direct exposure while its missile continued northward.","A0200":"A0200 maintained the northern approach beside and slightly west of A0100, descending and accelerating as the formations converged. It continued broadly northward through the simultaneous A0100/B0200 launch exchange, then expended a missile at 10.0 seconds and kept pressing ahead with only a modest rightward bias; this suggests an effort to sustain forward attack geometry or support its shot rather than immediately disengage, despite the B0200 missile already being recorded southbound.","B0100":"B0100 descended steadily southward from the opposing formation throughout the window, preserving a nearly constant southerly track while the A aircraft approached from below its flight path. Its ammunition decrease and the first appearance of a B0100 missile at 10.4 seconds indicate it joined the missile exchange after A0100 and A0200 had fired; continuing straight afterward most plausibly maintained pressure and launch geometry rather than signaling an evasive withdrawal.","B0200":"B0200 initially held a southbound, descending approach west of B0100, broadly aligned against the western A aircraft. At 9.4 seconds it expended a missile as an A0100 missile also appeared, then continued south with little lateral displacement while descending; this is most consistent with remaining committed to the head-on engagement and preserving attack pressure after launch, rather than executing an immediate defensive turn."}

{"A0100":"A0100 began a sustained right turn while descending, moving from a northbound approach into an easterly run; by the middle of the window it stopped further descent and stabilized on that easterly heading. With its own earlier-fired missile continuing north while both B missiles progressively angled toward A0100's side of the formation, this most plausibly represents a lateral defensive break to increase offset from the opposing pair and preserve separation rather than continuing directly into the head-on geometry.","A0200":"A0200 initially stayed near a northbound approach while descending, then progressively turned right and accelerated into a northeastward track, remaining below the opposing aircraft. Its previously present missile continued generally north, while the aircraft's widening eastward displacement from A0100 appears intended to avoid presenting the B formation with a compact, head-on pair and to retain an approach lane toward the western B aircraft rather than fully disengaging.","B0100":"B0100 maintained a steady southbound, descending advance throughout the window, broadly preserving its position as the eastern member of the B pair while accelerating. Its missile was already airborne and increasingly steered southeast as A0100 moved east, so the aircraft's continued approach most plausibly reflects sustained offensive pressure on the southern formation rather than a defensive withdrawal; no recorded maneuver indicates a change in that commitment.","B0200":"B0200 likewise continued a largely straight southbound descent and acceleration, holding the western side of the B formation rather than turning away as A0200 closed from the south. Its already-recorded missile also bent southeast over time, consistent with the ongoing exchange, while B0200's stable course appears intended to maintain forward pressure and preserve a useful opposing flank geometry rather than chase A0200 with a major aircraft maneuver."}

{"A0100":"A0100 maintained an almost straight eastbound, level acceleration throughout the window rather than turning toward either opponent. With its missile already in flight and both B aircraft initially north of its track, this most plausibly preserved separation and energy while allowing the pre-existing missile exchange to develop, rather than pursuing a new close-in attack. It continued this escape/repositioning line after B0200 became inactive; its ammunition count did not change within the window.","A0200":"A0200 began in a descending right turn from a northeastward course toward an east-southeast track, then made small heading corrections while continuing a sustained descent. This is most consistent with opening lateral and vertical separation during the ongoing reciprocal missile exchange, particularly as the two B missiles were traveling southeastward from ahead; it was not a direct pursuit of the northbound B formation. Its already-present missile converged near B0200 before both A missiles disappeared as B0200 became inactive, but the record cannot attribute that loss to a specific missile.","B0100":"B0100 initially held a nearly due-south, descending approach while its previously launched missile continued southeastward toward Team A. As B0200 disappeared and the two A missiles were removed, B0100 progressively curved left toward the southeast and continued descending, suggesting a break away from the original head-on geometry to gain lateral separation and survive after losing its teammate. Its missile remained recorded through the end, so the maneuver does not clearly indicate immediate disengagement from the missile exchange.","B0200":"B0200 descended rapidly while turning from south toward the southeast during the established missile exchange, a maneuver most plausibly intended to alter its exposure and relative geometry against the northbound A missiles while its own missile continued toward Team A. The turn did not produce a visible recovery: B0200 became inactive at 27.2 seconds as both A missiles were removed nearby. That timing is consistent with a terminal missile event, but does not establish the responsible missile or a confirmed hit mechanism."}

{"A0100":"A0100 initially maintained a fast, nearly level eastbound extension while the active B missiles remained northwest of it, without expending its own remaining weapon. From about 48.6 seconds it committed to a sustained left-hand turn, first climbing slightly and then descending sharply, which most plausibly represents a defensive lateral repositioning to reduce exposure and preserve separation rather than a direct attack: it did not turn toward a clear firing geometry or launch, while the opposing missile track was still in the area before disappearing.","A0200":"A0200 spent the entire window accelerating in a descending, increasingly northward-curving maneuver rather than holding its initial eastbound course. This is most plausibly an extended defensive response to B01001: that missile approached from the northwest, descended toward A0200's altitude band, and remained close behind its route through the end of the window; the turn and descent appear intended to create changing lateral and vertical geometry while escaping east-northeast, not to set up an attack.","B0100":"B0100 entered already out of missiles and continued descending southeast before progressively turning toward an easterly heading, bringing it onto a more direct pursuit line behind the withdrawing A aircraft. Its surviving missile, B01001, continued toward A0200 while B0100's own turn reduced the offset to that aircraft, suggesting an effort to maintain pressure and support the existing engagement rather than disengage; no outcome is established within the window.","B0200":"B0200 remained inactive with no valid flight data throughout the window, so no tactical intention can be inferred."}

{"A0100":"A0100 spent the first half of the window in a sustained descending left-hand reposition, curving from a northerly course toward the west while separating from the lower engagement. Once B0100 lay to its southwest, A0100 expended its final missile and then reversed into a sustained rightward turn, most plausibly breaking laterally away while the weapon continued toward B0100. The missile and B0100 were removed together later, which is consistent with the attack reaching its end but does not confirm a hit.","A0200":"A0200 maintained a fast, low-level northeastward displacement throughout, repeatedly commanding rightward adjustments that progressively curved its route rather than committing toward B0100. B0100's pre-existing missile remained behind and west of A0200 on a roughly similar northeast track, so this sustained maneuver most plausibly preserved lateral separation and denied a simple closing geometry while retaining speed. It continued this evasive or disengaging reposition after B0100 disappeared from the record.","B0100":"B0100 began with no missiles remaining but with one of its missiles already in flight, and initially flew east before settling onto a northeast course broadly toward Team A's lower aircraft, consistent with continuing or supporting that prior missile engagement. After A0100 launched, B0100 maintained its northeast escape while climbing sharply, a change most plausibly intended to create vertical separation from the incoming weapon. A0100's missile subsequently converged near B0100 before both records were removed, though the removal does not establish the cause.","B0200":"B0200 remained inactive with no valid flight data throughout the window, so no tactical intention can be inferred."}
